note: Axisflying publishes the AF2207.5 as one product in two windings (1860 and 1960 KV, one SKU with the KV chosen at checkout), and a Testing data sheet for each, so both windings are on this page; the RaceDayQuads listing we price from carries only the 1960 KV. Identity against that listing: 33.90 g with its 20AWG 150 mm leads, 6S, 1960 KV. Both sheets: 12N14P, 5 mm shaft with an M5 prop thread (13 mm exposed), 63.42 mOhm at 1860 KV and 61.49 mOhm at 1960 KV, idle current 1.23 A at 10 V on every prop and both windings. Motor internal temperature at full throttle, 37 degC ambient: 110/97/102 degC on the 1860 KV sheet (GF 51466 V2 / HQ MCK / HQ P3.5) and 102/106/105/108 degC on the 1960 KV one (GF 51366 V3 / GF 51466 V2 / HQ J37 / HQ J40). Two things recorded as the source prints them rather than repaired: the spec block states the size as "Phi 27.*20.45mm" with a digit missing after the decimal point - the dimension drawing on the same image prints Phi 27 +/-0.1 and 20.45 +/-0.3, which is where the published figure comes from - and the HQ P3.5 70% row reads 22972 rpm against 22505 at 60% and 26238 at 80%, a flat step while current and thrust rise normally. The drawing's mount callout is four M3 holes on a Phi 16 +/-0.05 bolt circle, i.e. an 11.3 mm square, not the 16x16 mm square 22xx motors usually take; it is left out of mount_mm, which holds square patterns. Each sheet's spec block states Max Power, Max current and Max force per prop, and all seven are that prop's own 100% row - so no prop block is missing from this transcription; four of the seven differ in the last printed digit only (33.64 A against the table's 33.65, 896.13/907.28/912.06 W against 896.14/907.29/912.07), and the block prints max force to 0.1 g where the table rounds to whole grams. Axisflying also sells a separate "Bando 2207.5" in the same two KV whose spec block is a different motor (58.08/58.13 mOhm, Phi 27.9x32.9 mm, 35.50/35.65 g); nothing here comes from it. That one is the Axisflying x SyncFPV x Supafly collaboration we publish at /motors/axisflying-x-supaflyfpv-x-syncfpv-2207-5/, and the shaft is no longer one of the figures that separates the two: its block says 4 mm, but the dimension drawing beside it calls out an M5 thread over a Phi 5 shaft, same as this motor

Finding the product page was the job, not transcribing it: the C157-2 is in none of the eight motor collections read 2026-09-18, and the store's own search (/search?q=C157) is what turned it up, at /products/motors-c157-2-4s, SKU A02010004. The sheet is one winding on one prop: 3750 KV on an HQT90-4P at 4S (16.00 V flat), nine throttle points (20-100%). The block's Max power / Max current are that run's own 100% row (506.56 W / 31.66 A), so the spec-block cross-check lands - every Axisflying sheet read so far - and all 9 rows pass the efficiency identity AND printed power = V x A. Max thrust is the 100% row's 670 g; weight_g (13.58 g, wire included) and max_cells (4S, the block's "Battery" line, the schema.org product name "Motors C157-2 4s" and the voltage the bench run holds) are the two fields that kept this motor queued. Three source facts recorded rather than repaired. First, the page's prose spec list is stale and the sheet is not: the body text, which RaceDayQuads reprints, gives "Motor mounting hole size: 3*M2 (Φ10mm)" (RDQ: 4xM2), "AWG 24#, 100MM", "Φ19*18.9MM" and "14.5g including 150MM cables", while the Specification block and the drawing beside it give four M2 holes on a Φ12 bolt circle, 22# 100 mm silicone line, Φ19*18.3 mm and 13.58 g wire included; the same prose ships "1x C157 motor" and "3x M2x4 screws" against a four-hole drawing, i.e. it is the first-generation C157's copy carried over. The block and the drawing are taken. Second, RPM falls across the top of the run - 26828 at 80%, 26014 at 90%, 23195 at 100% - while thrust rises 544 -> 623 -> 670 g and current 22.27 -> 31.66 A; every row's printed power and efficiency follow its own voltage, current and thrust exactly, so only the RPM column is odd. Third, the mount is four M2 on a Φ12 bolt circle, an 8.5 mm square, and here RaceDayQuads reprints it correctly as "4xM2 (Φ12mm)" - the same retailer published the C224's identical Φ12 callout as "Mounting Pattern: 12x12mm M2", so we now have one bolt circle rendered both ways by one shop - and mount_mm is left empty as on the other Axisflying pages. The block's "Wheelbase 1.5 mm" is Axisflying's template label for the shaft, as on the collaboration 2207.5, and the drawing's Φ1.5 stub agrees; the prop mounts on four M2 screws around a Φ5 boss, not on that shaft.

Identity against our retail listing is not a resemblance but the same block: 5000 KV, 9N12P, 12 mm stator diameter, 6 g, 3S-4S, 0.95 A idle at 10 V, 89 W max continuous power (3S), 125 mOhm internal resistance, 6 A max current (3S), 1.5-2 A max-efficiency band at >80% and a Phi 16.1x10.9 mm motor dimension - nine figures to the digit, so the sheet titled "GTS 1204" and our "GTS-V2 1204" are one motor. Stator length 4 mm. Three things are reproduced as printed rather than corrected: (1) the block's 89 W and 6 A maxima are labelled 3S and are the top row of NO row in this sheet's own table - its 3S (11.1 V) full-throttle run is 40.0 W at 3.6 A and its 4S (14.8 V) one 82.9 W at 5.6 A - so unlike the five RCinPower sheets read 2026-09-15 the spec-block cross-check does not land here, presumably because the maxima were measured on a prop this sheet does not tabulate; (2) the marketing banner on the product page heads the motor "1204 5200KV" while the data sheet, our retail listing and the page title all say 5000 KV, and nothing here is taken from the banner; (3) the sheet prints "Shaft Diameter: 2mm" where our retail listing prints 1.5 mm - the sibling GTS-V2 1202.5 listing spells the same motor family out as a "1.5mm press fit prop shaft" with a "2mm internal shaft", so the two figures are the two ends of one shaft, as the 2104 sheets also print; the retailer's prop-shaft figure is left in the shaft field and the manufacturer's named here. The temperature column is printed empty for all eight rows.

The T block is our retail listing to the digit (1800 KV, 12N14P, 21x4 mm stator, 3 mm inner / 1.5 mm outer shaft, 4-6S, 0.5 A idle at 10 V, 210 mOhm, 22.1 A, 530 W, 15.9 g with 3 cm wire), while the M2 block differs from it only in weight, 16 g, its shaft being threaded for an M2 prop mount; RCinPower's own family strip lists 2104 LIGHT and 2104 M2 as two products, so the M2 tables belong to a part we do not carry. Our listing sells the 1800 KV; the 3000 KV T sheet is included as published and is the 3-4S winding (0.9 A idle, 110 mOhm, 36.2 A, 580 W, same 15.9 g and same dimensions). Motor dimension Phi 25.35x13.8 mm, 12x12 mm four-bolt base mount, with a 5x5 mm four-hole pattern on the bell. Four things are reproduced as printed rather than corrected: (1) both blocks label their power and current maxima "3S" and neither run is 3S - the 1800 KV sheet's 530 W / 22.1 A is its GF5130*3 24 V (6S) full-throttle row exactly, and the 3000 KV sheet's 580 W / 36.2 A is its GF5130*3 16 V (4S) row, where the current matches exactly and the power is the table's 579.2 W rounded; (2) the screw size in both mount callouts ("4 x M?") is five pixels tall in the only image RCinPower publishes and is not legible, so the mount is recorded as its measured 12x12 mm span with no thread; (3) our retail listing prints "Motor Dimensions: 23.35x13.8mm" where all four manufacturer sheets and the dimensioned drawing print Phi 25.35x13.8 mm, so the manufacturer figure is the one published here; (4) the retail listing's 1.5 mm shaft is the outer (prop) shaft - the sheets print 3 mm inner and 1.5 mm outer. Temperature after 3 s at full throttle runs 52-78 degC on the 1800 KV sheet and 54-80 degC on the 3000 KV one, with the 3000 KV GF5130*3 16 V run flagged HOT

note: RCinPower builds the GTS V3 2105 Plus in 1850, 2950 and 3600 KV and publishes a data sheet for each; our retail listing covers the 2950 KV. The 1850 KV is the 5-6S winding and is benched at 21 V and 24 V; the 2950 and 3600 KV blocks rate the motor 3-4S and bench it at 12 V and 16 V. 12N14P, 21x5.5 mm stator, 3 mm inner shaft with an M5 prop thread, 12x12 mm four-bolt M2 mount, Phi 25.53x15.2 mm (the 3600 KV sheet prints 15.4 mm), internal resistance 160/60/45 mOhm for 1850/2950/3600 KV. Three things in the source are reproduced as printed rather than corrected: (1) the 2950 KV sheet benches its two Gemfan D76 duct props at 24 V - 6S on a motor its own block rates 3-4S - and the D76*5 full-throttle row draws 688.8 W against that block's 620 W max-continuous rating; (2) all three blocks head their power and current maxima "3S" even on the 5-6S 1850 KV, which is RCinPower's template label and not a 3S measurement; (3) the 3600 KV sheet leaves the HQ T5*3R 16 V rows blank. The 2950 KV sheet image is also clipped: the Gemfan 6026 16 V full-throttle row and the table footer are cut off, so that row is missing here - its block's 620 W and 38.8 A are 16 V x 38.8 A = 620.8 W, which is where it would have landed. Where the sheet is complete the same check passes exactly: the 1850 KV block's 396 W and 16.5 A are its Gemfan 6026 24 V full-throttle row, and the 3600 KV block's 582 W and 36.4 A are its Gemfan D90*3 16 V row. Weight is 20 g with 3 cm wire on the 1850 and 3600 KV sheets and 21 g on the 2950 KV one. Temperature after 3 s at full throttle runs 59-75 degC on the 1850 KV and 53-83 degC on the other two, with the 3600 KV Gemfan D90*3 16 V run flagged HOT; the 2950 KV Gemfan 6026 16 V temperature cell is clipped mid-glyph and is not readable

Four things in the source are reproduced as printed rather than corrected: (1) the two marketing banners on RCinPower's first product image head the motor "1920kv / 1980kv / 2500kv", which contradicts the three data sheets, the family comparison strip on the second image and our retail listing - all of which say 1980/2080/2480, so the banner is the odd one out and nothing here is taken from it; (2) all three blocks label their power and current maxima "5S", but on the 1980 and 2080 KV sheets the row those maxima name is the 24 V (6S) one - only the 2480 KV sheet's 5S label matches its own table; (3) two 21 V rows print 6.8 A beside 141.8 W and 142.8 W under the same heading, i.e. the current column is rounded and the power column is not; (4) the screw size in the mount callout ("4 x M?") is five pixels tall in the only image RCinPower publishes and is not legible, so the mount is recorded as its measured 16x16 mm span without a thread. Where the sheets are complete the spec block's own maxima are the top row of its table, on all three: 934 W / 38.9 A is the 1980 KV GF 5152 24 V full-throttle row, 1042 W / 43.4 A the 2080 KV HQ EthiX S5 24 V row, and 975 W / 46.4 A the 2480 KV GF 5152 21 V row. note: RCinPower publishes this motor at www.rcinpower.com/G-SERIES/40.html as "WASP MAJOR", three data sheets headed "Wasp Major - 22.6-6.5" at 1860, 2020 and 2420 KV. Identity against our retail listing is five figures shared to the digit: 22.6 mm stator diameter, 6.5 mm stator length, 30.5 g with 3 cm wire, and 1860 and 2420 KV both appearing as sheet titles. It is not the neighbouring product: the Wasp Major V2 (www.rcinpower.com/G-SERIES/67.html) is a 22.6-6.6 stator at 1980 and 2100 KV weighing 29.5 g, and the V2 King we publish separately is 2160 KV. 12N14P, 4 mm hollow shaft. The printed motor dimension Phi 28.49x30.6 mm is body plus shaft - the side view dimensions it as 18 mm plus 12.60 mm, which sum to the 30.6. Five things are reproduced as printed rather than corrected or guessed: (1) the three sheets give three cell ranges - 5~6S at 1860 and 2020 KV, 4~5S at 2420 KV - and are benched accordingly (21 and 24 V on the first two, 16 and 21 V on the third), while the retail listings we cite state 4-5S for the whole model; a multi-winding motor with no family cell count is an open question for this dataset, not something this entry decides. (2) The 2020 KV sheet tabulates the GF 6*4.5*2 at 21 V only - its two 24 V cells are printed empty - so that sheet carries 18 rows where the other two carry 20, and the missing run is named rather than interpolated. (3) The spec block's Max Continuous Power and Max Current, which on five earlier RCinPower sheets were the top row of that sheet's own table, land on no row here and are labelled 5S on all three sheets: 900 W / 35 A at 1860 KV against a 5S maximum of 573.3 W / 27.3 A, 920 W / 38 A at 2020 KV against 703.5 W / 33.5 A, and 970 W / 46 A at 2420 KV against 963.9 W / 45.9 A - only the last is close, and its current rounds while its power is 6 W out. (4) The mounting-hole callout on all three drawings is below the resolution RCinPower published - the two span dimensions are a smudge that 16 and 18 both fit - so no mount pattern is recorded, the same verdict the 2107 Plus thread got. (5) The sheet image is served under the filename "2207Pluschanpinyemian01", a name recycled from another product; every sheet inside it is titled Wasp Major 22.6-6.5, so the content was read and the filename ignored. Temperature after 5 s at full throttle, by sheet: 1860 KV 61-76 degC on 5S and 73-85 on 6S; 2020 KV 64-79 on 5S and 75-85 on 6S; 2420 KV 60-77 on 4S and 74-89 on 5S, with the 85, 86 and 89 degC runs flagged HOT on the sheets themselves. note: Champion Edition. Specs and bench data come from RCinPower's own product page. 12N14P, 22.6x6.6 mm stator, 4 mm hollow shaft, body 27.6x18.1 mm, 29.5 g with 3 cm wire, 48 mOhm, 1613 W continuous and 67.2 A max on 5S. Not sold by our retail source, so this entry is maintained by hand. RCinPower's sheet reports motor temperature after 5 s at full throttle: 61-72 degC on 5S and 77-90 degC on 6S, with the 51499 flagged as HOT. Two more windings of this motor come off www.rcinpower.com/G-SERIES/67.html, which RCinPower titles "WASP MAJOR 2": two sheets headed "Wasp Major V2 - 22.6-6.6" at 1980 and 2100 KV, 20 rows each, five props at 21 V and 24 V, 50% and 100% throttle. They are the same motor as the 2160 KV sheet at /68.html, which is headed identically plus "Champion Edition": all three print 12N14P, a 22.6 mm stator diameter, a 6.6 mm stator length, a 4 mm hollow shaft, a Phi 27.6x18.1 mm body, 29.5 g with 3 cm wire and 5~6S, and the internal resistance falls with KV across them - 56 mOhm at 1980, 52 at 2100, 48 at 2160 - which is one stator in three windings, so they share this page under the one-page-per-motor rule. Idle current at 10 V is 1.2 A at 1980 KV and 1.3 A at 2100 KV. Four things are recorded as printed rather than corrected: (1) both new sheets' spec blocks label Max Continuous Power and Max Current "5S", but the figures are that sheet's own 24 V full-throttle top row - 1337 W / 55.7 A at 1980 KV is the Gemfan 6032 24 V 100% run (1336.8 W, 55.7 A) and 1531 W / 63.8 A at 2100 KV is the Gemfan 51499 24 V 100% run (1531.2 W, 63.8 A) - so the cross-check lands on a row again, under the wrong cell count. (2) The prop set is not identical across the sheets: the fourth prop is a Gemfan 6032 at 1980 KV and a Gemfan 51499 at 2100 KV, while the 4934R, F4R, 51466 V2 and HQ MCK run on all three. (3) The sheets print prop names as "GF"; they are stored expanded to Gemfan, the way the 2160 KV rows already were, so one prop reads as one name across the table. (4) The drawings call out four M3 mounting holes, but the two span dimensions are a rotated two-digit smudge below the resolution RCinPower published, so no mount pattern is recorded - the same verdict the 22.6-6.5 and 2107 Plus sheets got. Temperature after 5 s at full throttle: 1980 KV 58-67 degC on 5S and 72-84 on 6S; 2100 KV 59-70 on 5S and 75-88 on 6S, with the 88 degC Gemfan 51499 run flagged HOT on the sheet. The page's peak stays the 2160 KV sheet's 2296 g; the new sheets peak at 2250 g (1980 KV, Gemfan 6032, 24 V) and 2158 g (2100 KV, Gemfan 51499, 24 V). Neither new winding is carried by our retail source; their rows are the manufacturer's and are labelled with their KV like the others

note: Bench rows, configuration and dimensions are from T-Motor's own "Test Report", "Specifications" and "Product Drawing" images on tmotorhobby.com/goods-1199.html. Identity with our retail listings is four figures shared to the digit - the 2808 stator, 12N14P, 60.5 g, which is the 1500 KV block's Weight (Incl. Cable), and both KV the retailers sell appearing as Specifications blocks and as report blocks. The block and the report carry a third winding, 1950 KV, which neither RaceDayQuads nor Pyrodrone lists and which T-Motor's own product name does not either - that name, "T-MOTORHOBBY VELOX V2808 Drone Motor", carries no KV at all - so kv_options gains it: 1300 KV is 61.1 g with a 1.19 A idle current at 10 V, 1500 KV 60.5 g and 1.49 A, 1950 KV 61.1 g and 2.45 A, all three 12N14P on a 4 mm shaft with an 18# 250 mm lead. Max thrust is the 1300 KV Gemfan GF8040-3 6S 100% row, 3083.4 g, where the page carried none. The spec-block cross-check lands on all three windings and is a second worked example of the maxima being per column rather than per row: on 1300 KV the block's Max. Power (10s) and Peak Current (10s) are one row (T7546-3 at 100%, 1511.9 W / 62.4 A) and on 1500 KV they are one row too (GF8040-3 at 100%, 1781.7 W / 74.3 A), but on 1950 KV the 1849.3 W is the T6143-3 100% row and the 82.3 A is the GF7040-3 one, two different prop runs. Every figure is printed in full rather than truncated or rounded, unlike the V3115's. All 60 rows pass the efficiency identity - printed thrust / printed power is the printed efficiency on every one - and printed power is voltage x current to within the band the one-decimal columns allow on all 60, with no run carrying an offset (the largest implied k is 0.12 A, on an 80 A row where the voltage column's own rounding allows 0.2 A), so nothing here has the V2208's or the V2306.5's constant. The Voltage column is a test voltage and not a rating: this template has no cell-range column at all, so the sheet adds no per-winding cell counts to argue with our 6S, and the runs themselves are at 25.2 V (6S) on both 1300 and 1500 KV and at 25.2 V, 21 V (5S) or 16.8 V (4S) depending on the prop at 1950 KV. Three source facts recorded rather than repaired. First, the Specifications block gives the Shaft Diameter as 4 mm where the drawing beside it calls out M5 on the threaded prop end, which is what our retailers' 5 mm agrees with - the same two-figure shaft the V2207 V3 block states explicitly as IN 4 mm / OUT 5 mm - so shaft stays 5 mm. Second, the HQ 5040-6 and Gemfan GF7040-3 1300 KV runs both print an efficiency that rises before it falls (2.63 then 2.73, and 3.53 then 3.67, at 20% and 40%), with every row internally consistent; no other run on the sheet does. Third, the eight report images are not in epoch order on the page - the second table tile is 1659077819815061 and the third 1659077819779168 - so a list sorted by filename splices the table in the wrong order, and because every tile boundary falls between a 100% row and a 20% row the seamless-join check cannot catch it; what catches it is the propeller column, whose label sits at the centre of its cell, so an unnamed block at a tile edge belongs to the label three blocks away. Mount is left unpublished for the same reason as on the V3115, V3120, V2208, V2306 V3 and V2207 V3: the drawing dimensions 19 between the top and bottom of the four M3 holes and 19 between the left and right ones, with no diameter symbol, which is a 19 mm bolt circle and a 13.4 mm square, not the 19x19 the mount column holds. Measuring the drawing confirms it - the hole centres span 0.586 of the body circle the same drawing labels o33.4, against the 0.569 a 19 mm bolt circle predicts and the 0.805 a 19x19 square would - and the same sheet prints the symbol on that body diameter while omitting it on the bolt circle, so the symbol's presence is a property of the callout and not of the template. Propeller names are as this sheet prints them (T6143-3, T7546-3, HQ5040-6, GF7040-3, GF8040-3), with the brand prefixed.

note: Bench rows, configuration, dimensions and winding resistances are from T-Motor's own "Test Report", "Specifications" and "Product Drawing" images on tmotorhobby.com/goods-1330.html, where the report's own Type column reads "V3115 KV400", "V3115 KV640", "V3115 KV900" and "V3115 KV1050". Identity with our retail listings is three figures shared to the digit - 113.1 g, which is the 900 KV block's Weight (Incl. Cable), a 5 mm shaft (block: IN5 OUT5) and both KV the retailers sell appearing as blocks and as Types. The block and the report carry two further windings, 400 and 1050 KV, which no retailer we price from lists and T-Motor's own page title does not either - that title names no KV at all - so kv_options gains both: 400 KV is 113.4 g at 145.38 mOhm with a 0.59 A idle, 640 KV 113.3 g at 67.13 mOhm and 1.10 A, 900 KV 113.1 g at 38.08 mOhm and 1.57 A, 1050 KV 112.7 g at 33.84 mOhm and 1.79 A. Max thrust is the 400 KV T10.5X5-3 12 S 100% row, 4817 g, where the page carried none. The spec-block cross-check lands on all four windings, and reading it row-by-row is what shows the field is a per-column maximum rather than a row: on 400, 640 and 900 KV the block's Max. Power (10s) and Peak Current (10s) are one row - T10.5X5-3 at 100% (1982 W / 41.84 A, 1927 W / 61.83 A, 1894 W / 83.30 A) - but on 1050 KV the 1903 W is the HQ 1045-3 100% row and the 83.6 A the HQ 9050-3 one (83.61 A), two different runs. The current is also truncated on three blocks (41, 83, 83.6) and rounded on the fourth (61.83 printed as 62). Four source facts recorded rather than repaired. First, five cells in the report are printed wrong and each is left unpublished rather than reconstructed: the 400 KV HQ1050-3 60% and 70% efficiencies and the 400 KV T10.5X5-3 60% one all print "0.0" where the row's own thrust and power give 4.3, 3.8 and 4.5 g/W, so efficiency_gw is empty on those three rows; and the 900 KV HQ1050-3 60% current prints "408.08" A on a row whose 582 W at 24 V is about 24 A, so current_a is empty there. Second, the 900 KV T10.5X5-3 6 S power column prints 14, 16 and 19 W at 60/70/80% against the ~573, ~843 and ~1161 W its own voltage and current give; the power column is not part of our schema, so those three rows carry every other figure and the defect is recorded here. Third, printed power is voltage x current within the half-unit band the integer Voltage column allows on 179 of the 180 rows; the one exception is the 900 KV HQ1050-3 70% row, whose 840 W over 35.77 A implies 23.48 V against a printed 24, missing the band by 0.02 V. The voltage x (current + k) offset check is not runnable on this sheet for the same reason as on the V3120: with Voltage and Power both printed as whole numbers, k = 0 and k = 1 A are equally consistent with every row. Fourth, the drawing writes three of its dimensions with a comma decimal separator (O19,00, O37,20, and 51,10) and one with a dot (17.5) on the same sheet, exactly as the V3120's does. Mount is left unpublished for the same reason as on the V3120, V2208, V2306 V3 and V2207 V3: the drawing calls out "O19,00" on a leader pointing at the bolt circle with "4*M3" beside it, a 19 mm bolt-circle diameter, not the 19x19 square the mount column holds. This sheet also dates the report template that the V3120 entry called a 2026 one: its images are dated 20231129 and carry the identical column set - ten throttle points in 10% steps, a Torque (N*m) column and an Operating Temperature column printing "/" on every block, with Voltage and Power rounded to whole numbers - so that template predates the 2024 V-series sheets rather than succeeding them, and what selects it is the big-prop V31xx line, not the date. The two sheets differ in one field: where the V3120 block prints "Rated Power" (a mid-throttle figure), this one prints "Max. Power (10s)", and the lead is 18AWG 250mm against the V3120's 16AWG. Propeller names are as this sheet prints them (T8.5X5-3, HQ9050-3, T9.5X5-3, HQ1045-3, HQ1050-3, T10.5X5-3), with the brand prefixed.

Three source facts recorded rather than repaired. First, this is a third T-Motor report template, newer than both the 2021 V2-era and the 2024 V3-era sheets (its images are dated 20260520): 10 throttle points in 10% steps, a Torque (N*m) column the older sheets do not have, an Operating Temperature column printing "/" on all eight blocks, and - the part that matters for checking - Voltage and Power rounded to whole numbers. The voltage x (current + k) offset check that the V2208 and V2306.5 sheets answered cannot be run here at all: every one of the 80 rows is consistent with its printed integer volts and watts being the rounded form of unprinted figures, and no offset can be either shown or ruled out at that resolution. Second, the prop sets differ between the windings and between voltages - HQ 1050-3, T10.5X5-3 and HQ 1145-3 all run at 48 V on the 500 KV winding with a second T10.5X5-3 run at 32 V, while on the 700 KV winding all three run at 32 V with a second T10.5X5-3 run at 24 V - and both tile joins were cropped and appended before that was accepted; the joins are seamless, with the merged Type cell's "V3120" and "KV500"/"KV700" landing on opposite sides of each boundary, so nothing is missing between the tiles. Third, the drawing writes three of its dimensions with a comma decimal separator (O19,00, O37,20, 56,10) and one with a dot (17.5) on the same sheet. Mount is left unpublished for the same reason as on the V2208, V2306 V3 and V2207 V3: the drawing calls out "O19,00" on a leader pointing at the bolt circle with "4*M3" beside it, a 19 mm bolt-circle diameter, not the 19x19 square the mount column holds. Identity with our retail listing is the 2208 stator, a 4 mm shaft, 6S and 33.4 g - the last being the 1950 KV winding's weight excluding cable, the block giving 36.9 g incl. / 33.1 g excl. at 1750 KV and 37.2 g / 33.4 g at both 1950 and 2450 KV - and both KV RaceDayQuads sells appear as blocks. The block and the report carry a third winding, 2450 KV, which neither the retailer nor T-Motor's own page title lists, so kv_options gains it; that winding is rated 4-5S and is benched at 4S, while max_cells stays 6S, the rating of the two 6S windings. The block's Max. Power (60s) / Peak Current (60s) is that winding's own 100% row, truncated rather than rounded: 796 W / 34.5 A is T5150 at 1750 KV (796.46 W / 34.50 A), 980 W / 43.2 A is T5147 at 1950 KV (980.16 W / 43.29 A) and 611 W / 40.3 A is T5150 at 2450 KV (611.79 W / 40.34 A), so the spec-block cross-check lands on all three. One source fact recorded rather than repaired, and it runs through the whole sheet: the Power column is not voltage x current but voltage x (current + a constant), and the constant is a property of the winding - 0.21 A at 1750 KV, 0.00 A at 1950 KV and 1.10 A at 2450 KV, each holding to +/-0.01 A across all 44 of that winding's rows. Every one of the 132 rows is exactly consistent with its own printed power and efficiency; at 2450 KV the missing 1.10 A is a large enough share of a low-throttle draw that 18 rows fall outside check_thrust.py's 6% band against voltage x current, and those are listed in ACCEPTED_EFF with the arithmetic. Mount is left unpublished for the same reason as on the V2306 and V2207 V3: the drawing calls out "Ø16" through two opposite holes with "4-M3" beside it, a 16 mm bolt circle (11.3 mm between consecutive holes), not the 16x16 square the mount column holds - and unlike the later V3 drawings (uploaded 2024), this 2021 one prints the Ø, which is what identifies the bare 16 on those as the same measurement. Propeller names are as this sheet prints them (T5143S, T5146, T5147, T5150); sibling T-Motor pages whose sheets printed the blade count instead carry the same props as "... Tri-Blade".

The block and the report carry a second winding, 2550 KV, which the retailer does not list, so kv_options gains it; that winding is rated 4-5S and is benched at 4S, while the 1950 KV one is rated 6S and benched at 6S. The block's Max. Power (60s) / Peak Current (60s) is that winding's own 100% row, truncated rather than rounded: 902 W / 37.4 A is T5146 at 1950 KV (902.36 W / 37.43 A) and 490 W / 33 A is T5147 at 2550 KV (490.07 W / 33.04 A), so the spec-block cross-check lands on both. The prop set differs between the windings - T4943, T5143S, T5146 and T5147 at 1950 KV, T5143S, T5146, T5147 and T5150 at 2550 KV - and both gaps were checked against the tile joins rather than assumed. Three source facts recorded rather than repaired. First, the Power column is voltage x current on 87 of the 88 rows but voltage x (current + 0.70 A) across all eleven rows of the 2550 KV T5146 run, a constant holding to +/-0.01 A; every row is exactly consistent with its own printed power and efficiency, and the three lowest-throttle rows of that run are the only ones where the missing 0.70 A is a large enough share of the draw to fall outside check_thrust.py's 6% band, so they are listed in ACCEPTED_EFF with the arithmetic. Second, the 1950 KV T5147 55% row draws 8.67 A against 50%'s 8.65 A and prints 211.90 W against 211.95 W - a current and power that barely move while thrust rises 752.63 -> 803.09 g and RPM 19309 -> 21823, which is why its 3.79 g/W is the highest efficiency in the winding and sits above the 50% row's 3.55. Third, the 1950 KV T5143S run reads 25.05 V at 50% and 25.06 V at 55% before falling monotonically, and it is the only run on the sheet whose voltage starts above 25 V. Mount is left unpublished for the same reason as on the V2208, V2306 and V2207 V3: the drawing calls out "Ø16" through two opposite holes with "4-M3" beside it, a 16 mm bolt circle, not the 16x16 square the mount column holds. Propeller names are as this sheet prints them (T4943, T5143S, T5146, T5147, T5150); sibling T-Motor pages whose sheets printed the blade count instead carry the same props as "... Tri-Blade".

The block's Max. Power (60s) / Peak Current (60s) is that winding's own 100% row on T-Motor T5147-3 at 1750 KV (814.3 W / 34.6 A), 1950 KV (1050.5 W / 45.0 A), 2050 KV (1153.4 W / 49.5 A) and 2550 KV (642.5 W / 41.8 A); at 1500 KV the Max. Power cell prints 1915.1, which is the F5146-3 100% row's thrust in grams rather than its 1050.5 W power, while the 33.3 A beside it is that row's current - the same mislabelled cell as the V2306 V3 sheet. T5143S-3 and T5147-3 are benched at four windings each, not five: neither has a 1500 KV block, and the report's image tiles were joined edge to edge to confirm the gap is the manufacturer's and not a clipped image. All 100 rows match the efficiency printed beside them when it is taken against the sheet's own power column; three - the 10% points on T6143-3, C7.5X4.6X3 and GF7042-2 - do not when power is recomputed as voltage x current, because current is printed to 0.1 A and those rows draw 0.1-0.2 A (the sheet prints 3.9, 2.1 and 4.3 W). Three further low-current rows - F5146-3 at 20%, T6143-3 at 20% and 30% - miss that recomputed power by 2-6% for the same reason while passing the efficiency check. Mount is left unpublished: the drawing calls out 4-M3 with a plain 16 between the top and bottom holes and a plain 16 between the left and right holes, and the four holes sit at 90 degrees on that circle, so the figure is a 16 mm bolt circle (11.3 mm between consecutive holes), not the 16x16 square the mount column holds.
